Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-long-0061", "row_sha256": "b30f4acfb2561bb31767dbfef0aa38f10c213455cfe5bf8be8320d2e86055836", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "hey, can you help me write a clear prompt for making a registration page for the Cedar Quay Open chess tournament? this should be a page in the small website we already have, not a whole new site. use the existing HTML and CSS files if you need to describe how it should fit in; do not install packages. you can reorganize the details below, but the page needs to be easy for a player or parent to scan and understand. I want the result to include the actual page text and a simple description of the sections and form fields, not a finished tournament announcement or an answer to players asking whether they are registered.

the event is the Cedar Quay Open, a one-day chess tournament on Saturday, September 18, 2027, at Cedar Quay Community Hall, 18 Alder Street, Port Rowan. doors open at 8:15 a.m. and the first round starts at 9:00 a.m. the schedule is five rounds using a Swiss pairing system, with a time control of 15 minutes plus a 10-second increment per move. include those details together so people don't mistake the doors-open time for the start time. the event is open to players of all ages and experience levels, and a US Chess membership is not required. don't imply that it is divided into rating or age sections; the tournament has one open section.

registration is limited to 64 players. the entry fee is $25 per player and is payable in cash at check-in; there is no online payment option. registration closes at 6:00 p.m. on Wednesday, September 15, or earlier if all 64 places are filled. if the limit is reached first, later entries should be described as a waitlist rather than confirmed seats. please make that condition visible near the registration action and don't say that submitting the form guarantees a place. players should arrive by 8:40 a.m. to check in. someone who has registered but has not checked in by 8:40 may lose their place to a waitlisted player, but only if a waitlisted player is present. phrase that carefully, since it isn't an automatic cancellation in every case.

for the form, ask for the player's full name, age, email address, and phone number. also ask whether they have a US Chess rating, and if yes, provide a box for the rating number; an unrated player should still be able to submit the form. include a field for an optional note about access needs. if a player is under 16, ask for a parent or guardian's name and contact email as well. don't make those extra fields mandatory for older players. don't ask people to enter payment card information, because the fee is paid in cash at check-in. make clear that one form is for one player, so a family registering several players should submit a separate form for each person.

we need the page to explain what happens after submission without claiming that a spot has been reserved. the organizer will email each person to confirm receipt and say whether there is an available seat or whether they are on the waitlist. the tournament contact email is chess@cedarquay.org. please show that address as the contact for questions and access requests. the page should not promise a response time that we haven't provided. there is no need to invent a phone contact for the organizer just because the registration form collects the player's phone number.

include the location and practical arrival details in a separate section. the hall is at 18 Alder Street, Port Rowan; free parking is available in the hall's rear lot, and the entrance on Alder Street has a step-free route. players may bring their own chess set and clock, but the tournament will have sets and clocks available to share, so don't present bringing equipment as compulsory. food is not provided. there is a café across the street, but it may not be open during the event, so say players should plan their own lunch rather than treating the café as a guaranteed option. don't add directions, transit information, or venue facilities we haven't listed.

there is one short quote from the organizer that i want included exactly as spoken, preferably near a welcome line: “We’re glad to have first-time players and regular tournament players at the same boards.” keep it as an ordinary welcome, not a promise about prizes or coaching. don't invent prizes, awards, cancellation terms, refunds, or a tournament director's name. If any part of the page needs to mention those topics, leave them out rather than filling in details.

maybe lay the page out in this order: 1. event name and welcome, 2. date, venue, and schedule, 3. who can enter and the fee, 4. registration form and the 64-player limit, 5. check-in and waitlist information, then 6. location and practical notes. use clear headings and compact wording, but not so compressed that the deadline and the earlier-full condition get lost. make the registration action easy to find. include a note that registration details are used to administer this event and contact the person registering, and that email addresses and phone numbers won't be shown on a public player list. keep the final page useful on its own while making it clear that a submitted form is not the same as an organizer's confirmation of a seat.", "output": "Create a clear, easy-to-scan registration page for the Cedar Quay Open chess tournament within the existing website. Use the existing HTML and CSS files if you describe how the page should fit into the site; do not install packages. Provide the page copy and a simple description of its sections and form fields. Do not write a tournament announcement or respond to individual registration questions.

Organize the page with clear headings and compact wording, using this order:
1. Event name and welcome
2. Date, venue, and schedule
3. Eligibility and entry fee
4. Registration form and player limit
5. Check-in and waitlist information
6. Location and practical notes

The event is the Cedar Quay Open, a one-day tournament on Saturday, September 18, 2027, at Cedar Quay Community Hall, 18 Alder Street, Port Rowan. Doors open at 8:15 a.m.; the first round starts at 9:00 a.m. The tournament has five Swiss-system rounds with a time control of 15 minutes plus a 10-second increment per move. The event is open to players of all ages and experience levels. A US Chess membership is not required, and there is one open section, not separate rating or age sections.

The entry fee is $25 per player, payable in cash at check-in. There is no online payment option. Registration closes at 6:00 p.m. on Wednesday, September 15, or earlier if all 64 places are filled. Make the 64-player limit and the early-full condition visible near the registration action. If the limit has been reached, describe later entries as waitlisted, not as confirmed seats. Do not imply that submitting a form guarantees a place.

Ask each player for their full name, age, email address, and phone number. Ask whether they have a US Chess rating, and show a field for the rating number only if they answer yes; unrated players must still be able to submit the form. Include an optional note field for access needs. For players under 16, ask for a parent or guardian’s name and contact email; do not make these fields mandatory for older players. Do not request payment card information. State that one form is for one player and that families registering several players should submit a separate form for each person.

Explain that the organizer will email each person to confirm receipt and say whether a seat is available or the person is on the waitlist. Do not promise a response time or claim that form submission reserves a place. Players should arrive by 8:40 a.m. to check in. A registered player who has not checked in by 8:40 may lose their place to a waitlisted player only if a waitlisted player is present; make clear that this is not an automatic cancellation in every case.

Show chess@cedarquay.org as the contact for questions and access requests. Do not invent an organizer phone number. Include a note that registration details are used to administer the event and contact the person registering, and that email addresses and phone numbers will not be shown on a public player list.

For location and practical notes, state that the hall is at 18 Alder Street, Port Rowan, has free parking in the rear lot, and has a step-free route at the Alder Street entrance. Players may bring their own chess set and clock, but the tournament will have sets and clocks available to share; do not describe personal equipment as compulsory. Food is not provided. A café across the street may not be open during the event, so advise players to plan their own lunch without presenting the café as a guaranteed option. Do not add directions, transit information, or unprovided venue facilities.

Include this organizer quote exactly as written, preferably near the welcome: “We’re glad to have first-time players and regular tournament players at the same boards.” Treat it as a welcome, not as a promise of prizes or coaching. Do not invent prizes, awards, cancellation terms, refunds, or the tournament director’s name; leave those topics out.

Keep the final page useful on its own and make clear that a submitted form is not the same as an organizer’s confirmation of a seat."}]
